STEP 1 - Scene: A small portion of roasted sweet potato cubes on a white square plate, photographed from above at a near-overhead angle, on a glass surface.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The plate is a square side plate, roughly 20 cm across. Vessel area ≈ 20 x 20 ≈ 400 cm^2 (the plate's rounded corners reduce this slightly; use ~360 cm^2 as the usable area).

STEP 3 - Items: Roasted sweet potato pieces (about 6-7 cubes, roughly 2-3 cm each), plus a small smear of orange glaze/oil residue near the right side.

STEP 4 - Area: Sweet potato cubes cover about 12% of the plate (~43 cm^2). Glaze/oil residue about 1% (~4 cm^2). Total covered ~13%.

STEP 5 - Volume: Sweet potato pile: 43 cm^2 x ~2 cm average height ≈ 86 ml. Each cube is about 2.5 cm x 2.5 cm x 2 cm ≈ 12 ml, times ~7 pieces ≈ 85 ml, consistent. Glaze residue is negligible volume (~1 ml).

STEP 6 - Grams: Sweet potato cubes: 86 ml x 0.6 g/ml ≈ 52 g (cut vegetable density; roasted pieces are fairly dense, so 52 g is reasonable). Glaze/oil residue ≈ 1 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Roasted sweet potato ≈ 90 kcal/100 g. 52 g x 0.9 ≈ 47 kcal. Glaze/oil residue ≈ 1 g x 300 kcal/100 g (sugary glaze) ≈ 3 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Seven small cubes of roasted sweet potato, about 50 g and roughly 50 kcal, is plausible for what is visible. The residue is minor.
